messages:
maria: Heads-up — spotted sustained memory growth on node gpu-12 while running long-context billing workloads. KV residency for tenant-42 keeps creeping even after requests finish. :eyes:

ajay: Can you paste the top /proc/mem and the kv residency dump?

maria: quick snapshot: `pmap -x /proc/12345` shows lots of anonymous pages attributed to kv-cache. Also `kvctl dump --tenant=42 --pages=recent` => many pages with small refcounts but not being freed. Paste logs:```
[2026-03-15 14:12:01] tenant=42 page=0x7f9a3c ref=1 last_used=14:03:21 flags=SLAB_SMALL owner=kv_cache
[2026-03-15 14:12:03] tenant=42 page=0x7f9a72 ref=0 last_used=14:04:00 flags=FRAGMENTED owner=kv_cache
[2026-03-15 14:12:05] tenant=42 page=0x7f9b81 ref=0 last_used=14:05:03 flags=GHOST owner=kv_cache
```

kai: hmm "GHOST" flag — that's our marker for pages we believe are logically evictable but remain pinned due to longctx tail pointers. Are these all large-key slots?

maria: mix of key sizes. The common factor seems to be long ctxs from tenant-42 using streaming chat with aggressive chunking. Sequence length distribution skewed high.

selina: sounds like fragmentation + partial reuse. When we drop small slots we don't coalesce, so slabs become less usable and eviction pumps up. Could explain the apparent memory leak.

ajay: any perf regressions correlated? kernel selection or batching changes recently?

maria: we rolled the batching heuristic change last week (prefer batch-by-model then by length). No other runtime kernel changes. But I profiled `kv_pagewalk` with `perf` and saw increased CPU in `page_scan_slowpath` compared to baseline.

kai: can you include a `perf script` sample? also what's the eviction policy — pure LRU or our weighted quota?

maria: short `perf top` dump:```
50.1% kv_page_scan_slowpath
12.3% slab_free_try
8.7% page_reclaim
6.2% scheduler
```
We currently use weighted LRU with per-tenant watermarks but the watermark for tenant-42 seems not triggering because allocator thinks pages still referenced (refcounts > 0 for short bursts).

selina: idea — implement a generational eviction pass: promote pages on repeated hits, after one generation mark; if longctx hasn't touched them after X seconds, treat as stale and force reclaim ignoring small transient refs. This would reduce ghost accumulation.

kai: +1. Also we should add a "tail-sample" GC to detect longctx pinned pointers: sample the KV handles retained by in-flight longctxs and decrement a sticky pin if they're older than Y. Might be safer than forcible steal.

ajay: how about per-tenant low-priority eviction lanes? e.g., when global memory pressure > threshold, allow tenants with sustained high residency to be throttled or bumped to a slower model variant. That ties into our smart routing.

maria: that would help at the infra level. For now I want a small, deployable mitigation: (1) enable generational eviction on one canary host, (2) add a TTL-based soft-unpin for pages with GHOST flag > 30s, (3) collect telemetry (per-tenant residency, reclaim rate, page fragmentation).

ops-bot: Incident alert: gpu-12 memory pressure crossed 85% at 14:18 — autoscaler flagged burst.

kai: can we run the canary on gpu-12? good testbed. If generational pass reduces `kv_page_scan_slowpath` CPU and reclaims ghost pages, roll to the pool.

selina: I'll draft the canary patch. Quick pseudo:```
for page in candidate_list:
  if page.generation == 0 and hit_count == 0:
    page.generation = 1
  elif page.generation == 1 and last_used > TTL:
    force_reclaim(page)  // bypass weak refs for soft-unpin
```
We'll also emit `ghost_age` and `slab_frag_pct` metrics.

maria: test plan: run 4h replay of tenant-42 trace on canary with high longctx workloads, measure: resident_pages, reclaim_rate, page_scan_cpu, fragmentation. Baseline from last week attached.

ajay: also add a regen of compact_slab on low-priority background thread to coalesce small free fragments. Might reduce fragmentation spikes.

kai: watchouts — forced reclaim might momentarily increase latency for in-flight requests if we accidentally steal a live KV used by a pinned op. Need histograms of `steal_latency` and fallback penalties.

selina: agree. We'll gate the canary behind `evict_mode=soft` vs `evict_mode=force` and start with soft-unpin only.

maria: thanks team. I'll push telemetry dashboards and the tenant-42 replay. Can we meet 11:30 for a quick 15m sync after 2h of canary? :thumbsup:

kai: 11:30 works. Thanks.

ajay: ping me if ops-bot trips again.

ops-bot: Note: scheduled canary job created by selina at 14:25 (job-id cj-2026-03-15-14-25).
